item.title: UK: Iran 'highly likely' to be behind RAF Fairford incident
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham told parliament there were "strong indications" of Iranian involvement. The government summoned Iran's ambassador. The scare at RAF Fairford led to the withdrawal of USAF B-1 heavy bombers.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Poland reports arrests of 2 Turkish citizens in Germany in connection with Starlink station fire last month
item.description: Polish authorities have reported the arrests of two Turkish citizens in Germany in connection with alleged sabotage of a Starlink station last month. Prime Minister Donald Tusk called the fire an act of "hybrid warfare."
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Fact check: Viral videos falsely linked to Riyadh airport attacks
item.description: Many videos claiming to show an attack on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport have gone viral online. DW Fact check analyzes some of the most-shared footage and finds evidence it was created using AI.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Starlink India launch: Why Elon Musk is still waiting
item.description: Despite securing key approvals, the Starlink satellite internet service remains in regulatory limbo, raising questions about security clearances, competition and India’s investment climate.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Can South Korea and Ukraine resolve their diplomatic spat over North Korean POWs?
item.description: Seoul and Kyiv are trading accusations after the transfer of two North Korean POWs to South Korea. The South insists the move was to be kept secret as it seeks to avoid antagonizing Pyongyang.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Cyprus closer than ever to joining Schengen but political hurdles relating to the Green Line and British Sovereign Base Areas remain
item.description: The European Commission says Cyprus is ready to join the Schengen Area. Yet questions relating to the island's division and British military bases could still complicate its path to Europe's border-free travel zone.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Hurricane Simon batters Mexico's Pacific Coast
item.description: Hurricane Simon is currently running parallel to Mexico's Pacific Coast, bringing heavy rainfall and strong winds to vulnerable towns.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Two high-ranking Iranian defectors give DW a rare look into the mindset of the regime's loyal servants
item.description: Months of correspondence with two high-ranking defectors have given DW's investigative unit a rare look at the mindset of the regime's loyal servants — and revealed a clandestine circle that allegedly plots murders.
item.dc:subject: TOP STORIES

item.title: Air strikes kill dozens of gold miners on Sudan-Egypt border
item.description: A Sudan-based rights group said 72 people were killed in a remote, disputed area known for illegal gold mining.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Who are the Ukrainian 'volunteers' under Russian command?
item.description: Russia has announced a battalion consisting of Ukrainian "volunteers." But veterans and former prisoners of war share very different accounts.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Trump claims Russia and Ukraine agreed to 'energy ceasefire'
item.description: US President Donald Trump says both sides have agreed to stop targeting oil refineries, power plants and other energy infrastructure immediately.
item.dc:subject: News

item.title: Surrogacy in Georgia is booming but at what cost?
item.description: Georgia became a hub for surrogate pregnancies after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. DW spoke with parents, and those who wanted to become parents, about the hidden costs of a booming industry.
item.dc:subject: World

item.title: Money, networks and bias: Why women struggle to win seats in US politics
item.description: The US is holding Congress and state governor elections. At all levels of US politics, women are underrepresented — but they may win some historic victories in the midterms on November 3.
